facts.text: Woodridge sits in Ward 5 of Northeast Washington, D.C., a residential neighborhood that feels like a quiet enclave amid the city.
The neighborhood is bounded by Eastern Avenue NE to the south, Taylor Street NE to the west, South Dakota Avenue NE to the north, and Bladensburg Road NE to the east.
Rhode Island Avenue NE and Bladensburg Road NE form Woodridge’s main commercial strips, where local shops and eateries line the streets.
Woodridge residents can hop on the Metro at either the Brookland‑CUA or Rhode Island Avenue stations, giving easy access to downtown and beyond.
Every first Tuesday from September through June, the Woodridge Library hosts a community meeting from 6:30 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at 1801 Hamlin Street.
The Woodridge Civic Association documents the history of the neighborhood’s subdivisions, including Avalon Heights, Langdon, Montello, Woodridge, and Winthrop Heights.
